response.text:
Journal 2489 is a manual accrual (DR 5200 4868.32; CR 2100 2434.16 and CR 1200 2434.16). It balances, so the amounts are not in error. The only problem is that it sits in closed period 4 with a post date after that period's close. Posted rows can't be edited and a closed period can't be posted to, so the fix is to move the entry into an open period. That means reversing it out of period 4 and re-booking it in an open period.

A reversal posted in an open period would leave period 4 unchanged, so the net effect would not move the entry out of period 4. The correction lines also all have to go in one open period. The best available option is therefore to book the entry in open period 11, the earliest open period. Doing that alone would double count the expense, because the original lines stay in period 4. The ledger has no period-level balance table, though, and the original plus my lines must net to the right position in total.

The accrual's true economic position is that the original posting was invalid, since it was made after close. I read "move the affected accounts to their true position" as nulling the late entry. I would reverse it in open period 11 (CR 5200 4868.32, DR 2100 2434.16, DR 1200 2434.16). That nets the original and the correction to zero and keeps the correction as small as the finding allows. No invoice statuses change.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 2489 balances but was posted on 20240516 into period 4, which closed on 20240505, so it is outside the period dates and after close. A closed period can't be posted to and posted rows can't be edited, so I reverse the full journal in open period 11, the earliest open period. The reversal nets the original to zero (CR 5200 4868.32; DR 2100 2434.16; DR 1200 2434.16). The correction group balances. No invoice status changes.
